newsitem.title: USA: Phila. mob boss wins acquittal in murder retrial.
newsitem.headline: Phila. mob boss wins acquittal in murder retrial.

text.p: Jailed mob boss Nicodemo (Little Nicky) Scarfo was acquitted on Thursday on state charges he ordered the 1985 murder of an associate who was disrespectful.

Scarfo, who is serving a 55-year federal sentence for racketeering on top of a 14-year term for extortion, was given a second trial by an appeals court ruling of prosecutorial misconduct in the first trial.
After a two-week trial in Common Pleas court, the jury deliberated for just two hours -- including a lunch break -- before returning its verdict.

The murder of bookmaker Frank (Frankie Flowers) D'Alfonso on a South Philadelphia street was an outgrowth of the bitter fued that started with the 1979 assassination of then-mob boss Angelo Bruno. The violence propelled Scarfo to the top of the Philadelphia organised crime family and then led to his prosecution.

The government relied on the testimony of two former mobsters who testified that they killed D'Alfonso on Scarfo's order and with the assistance of five co-defendants who were also acquitted. All are serving other jail terms.
